subject: Banking
title: How FICO Scores Work
description: Learn How FICO Scores Work in one minute.

hook.text: FICO scores are used in 90% of US lending decisions. Five factors determine your number.

buildup.text: Payment history is 35%. Amounts owed is 30%. Length of credit history is 15%. New credit is 10%. Credit mix is 10%.

discovery.text: One late payment can drop your score 100 points. Paying on time is the single most important factor in your credit life.

twist.text: A closed card can hurt your score, and carrying a balance does not help despite the myth.

climax.text: Five factors, one formula, and nearly all lending decisions in America run through it.

punchline.text: 35% is payment history. Pay on time. That's the biggest factor.

quiz.question: What is the most important factor in a FICO score?

details.summary: FICO scores range from 300 to 850 and are calculated from five weighted factors: payment history at 35 percent, credit utilization at 30 percent, length of credit history at 15 percent, credit mix at 10 percent, and new credit inquiries at 10 percent.
details.whyItMatters: FICO scores are used in over 90 percent of US lending decisions. A score difference of just 50 points can mean tens of thousands of dollars more or less in interest over a mortgage's lifetime, making FICO one of the most consequential numbers in yo.
takeaways: Payment history and utilization together account for 65 percent of your score
FICO scores range from 300 to 850 with 670 and above considered good
Over 90 percent of US lenders use FICO scores for credit decisions

faq.question: Why are there multiple versions of FICO scores?
faq.answer: FICO regularly updates its scoring models, and different lenders use different versions. Auto lenders, credit card issuers, and mortgage lenders each have industry-specific FICO variants. You may have dozens of different FICO scores simultaneously.

faq.question: How quickly can you raise your FICO score?
faq.answer: Reducing credit utilization can improve your score within one billing cycle. Removing an error through a dispute takes 30 days. Adding positive payment history takes months. Recovering from major negative events takes years of consistent behavior.
